title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness, starvation prevention, and timeouts
author: Ava Chen
commits: scheduler: add per-priority queueing buckets and aging weights
scheduler: introduce request-timeout and preemption thresholds
kv-cache: add soft-prefetch hints for long-lived prefixes
tests: add fairness and starvation regression tests
docs: scheduler tuning notes and knobs
description: Motivation: continuous-batcher intermittently starved low-priority long-lived requests when high-priority short requests dominated the runqueue; customers saw tail latency variance under mixed workloads. This PR implements queueing buckets with aging-based weight adjustments, request-level timeouts and soft-preemption to prevent starvation, and KV-cache prefetch hints to reduce cold-prefix stalls. Changes include a bounded per-priority queueing structure, an aging factor that increases weight for waiting requests over time, a configurable preemption threshold that allows low-cost preemptions of high-priority inflight batches when starvation is detected, and request-timeout/abort paths to ensure long-blocked requests don't hold resources indefinitely. The KV cache introduces a soft-prefetch hint attached to request metadata that triggers low-priority prewarming of nearby KV shards for long-running conversational prefixes. Benchmarks: internal microbench shows 12% throughput improvement for mixed-chat workloads, P95 latency for low-priority class reduced from 820ms to 420ms under synthetic skew (90% high-priority short + 10% low-priority long), and tail variance significantly reduced. Deployment plan: feature-flag gated, gradual rollout to Dedicated fleet with observability dashboards and alerting for new metrics (scheduler.age_ratio, scheduler.preempt_count, kv.prefetch_hits). Backwards compatibility: config knobs default to previous behavior and are off for older clusters. See linked Linear items for rollout timeline and canary checklist.
